Commentary.Commentary: Right then. Pakistan have a lead of 158 runs, which is a very good one and with the pitch misbehaving, they could do some serious damage to the batting line-up of the visitors. South Africa will hope to bat well and cut down the deficit without losing a lot of wickets. An interesting essay of play coming up. Join us for the South African batting innings very shortly.

South Africa started off with the ball in superb fashion. They had some overs to play with on Day 1 and they removed 4 off the batters and ended the day in top fashion. But then came Day 2, they were made to toil and toil hard, at that. The duo of Azhar Ali and Alam did not make their job easier and after a lot of hard work, they have been able to dismiss the batters of Pakistan. Rabada and Maharaj scalped 3 wickets each, whereas, Nortje and Ngidi collected two wickets each. Overall, they could have been better with the ball.

Not quite the start that  Pakistan were looking for, in the first innings. After losing 4 quick wickets, they were reeling at 33/4 at the end of Day 1. But then, it was the revival job done by Azhar Ali and Fawad Alam and then the duo of Alam and Ashraf, during which Alam reached his century as well. He kept going on and on and on, even though he kept losing wickets at the other end. Towards the end, Yasir and Nauman also stitched a 55-run stand for the last wicket and it is due to their combined efforts, that Pakistan have ended their first innings with a lead of 158.

Pakistan, definitely would be the happier side heading into this break. They batted really well after their meltdown at the start and they finished strong as well courtesy of their tailenders and now lead by 158 runs.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 3 of this absorbing first Test between Pakistan and South Africa. Day 2 was all about the efforts of both the players whose name starts with the letter 'F'. Yes, you guessed it right. Fawad Alam and Faheem Ashraf (also with contributions from Azhar Ali and Mohammad Rizwan), which has seen Pakistan take the ascendancy in this game. They ended Day 2 with a lead of 88 runs to their name and will be looking to extend their lead to something around the 125-run mark, as they have just 2 wickets in hand. South Africa, meanwhile, would be hoping to finish the tail off quickly and keep the lead below 100. Which team is able to grab the third day, which is also known as the moving day, by the throat? Join us as we find out all the answers.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

So that is it from Day 2! Pakistan started the day fearing the worst but end it in the driver's seat. They will be mightly pleased with how things panned out on Day 2. Make sure you join us for Day 3 in this exciting contest between Pakistan and South Africa. The action on Day 3 begins at 1000 local (0500 GMT). We hope to see you then. Till then, goodbye and take care!

A chalk and cheese day for the bowlers as compared to Day 1. 14 wickets fell on Day 1 while just 4 wickets fell in the whole of Day 2. South Africa were made to work all day and their patience, calmness, and stamina were all put to test today. The Proteas bowlers toiled hard and tactically the tourists got a few crucial things wrong. The strategy to bowl one spinner from one end with the second new ball was an interesting one but a strategy that did not reap the desired result. Ngidi scalped 2 wickets today while Nortje and Maharaj got one apiece in the day. The South African bowlers will look to wrap this up early tomorrow and hope the batters can give them the rest they need on Day 3.

Pakistan started the day with their hearts in their mouth and in a state fearing the worst. They started at 33/4 but the experience of Azhar Ali and the calm-headedness of Fawad Alam got them back in this game. They battled the first session without losing a wicket. The pair added 94 runs for the 5th wicket with Azhar scoring a fifty. Rizwan then gave him decent support before departing. Fawad continued his battle and along with Faheem wiped the hosts' deficit and took them in the lead. The southpaw scored his first international Test ton on his home ground. That along with Faheem's 64 tired the South African bowlers and put the hosts in the driver's seat.

A very good day of Test cricket for Pakistan. They started the day in a very precarious position but have completely changed the tide of the game. The day belonged mainly to one Pakistani batter, whose hard work, perseverance, and determination saw him come back to the national team after a decade and today those qualities saw him hit his first ton in Pakistan and put his side in the ascendency. It was Fawad Alam's day and he deserves all the credit and plaudits that will come his way!

We are back for the final session of Day 2! The South African players are on the field taking their respective positions. Fawad Alam walks out with Faheem Ashraf to continue their innings. George Linde to bowl the first over of the final session.
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

A much-better session for South Africa. They toiled hard and finally found some rub of the green in this session. Keshav Maharaj got the better of Azhar Ali. Rabada and Ngidi bowled well and the latter too finally got his reward. The tourists though have lost all their reviews. But the wicket of Rizwan right towards the end should energize the Proteas bowlers and they will look to carry some momentum in the final session of the day. Can they bowl out Pakistan before they cross the deficit or will Pakistan get the lead? Join us in the final session to find out.

Good session of cricket for both sides. Pakistan started off well with Azhar Ali and Fawad Alam continuing from where they left off. The former departed right after getting to his fifty but the latter is still battling out in the middle. He stitched a solid stand with Rizwan who was looking good but departed in the final over before Tea. The hosts still trail by 42 runs and will hope Fawad Alam can continue his merry ways while Faheem can support him.

Ali is nimble on his feet and he works it to long on for one.
A shortish ball on off, Ali stands tall and guides it towards point. A single taken.
Good length on middle, Ali solidly defends this on the on side.
Short again but down the leg again, Ali is not interested in playing that.
Fullish on middle and leg, Ali tucks this towards mid-wicket and thinks for a run but Bavuma there does well to dive and field the ball. Stops the single.
Shortish but down the leg side, Ali shuffles and lets it go to the keeper.
Good length around off, Ali blocks this out back towards the bowler.
Shortish around off, Alam keeps it towards mid-wicket. 2 runs from Maharaj's first over this morning.
Floated on middle, Ali plays it softly towards covers and takes a quick single.
Flatter around off, driven towards mid off for nothing.
Fullish on middle, Ali dances down the track and pushes it past the bowler towards mid on.
Floated around off, Alam sweeps it down to fine leg for a single.
Fuller around off, Alam defends this out off the front foot.

DRINKS! Pakistan's hour! They have not lost a wicket and have also added some handy runs. The wicket too looks a little easier to bat on that it was yesterday and the key has been the rotation of strike. More of the same is what they would want. South Africa on the other hand, need to break this partnership. Can they do so? We will find out. Keshav Maharaj comes onto bowl now. Spin for the first time today.
A length ball around off, bounces a little too much as Ali is rapped on the gloves here. He does well to keep it down on the leg side.
Sharp bouncer on middle, Ali ducks under it.
Quick run. A length ball around off, Alam turns this one softly towards long on and calls his partner for a quick run.
Bowls a good length around off, Alam blocks this on the leg side.
That one keeps low now. A length around off, Alam defends thiis off the toe end towards first slip.
A length ball on middle, Alam looks to work it on the leg side but gets a leading edge which goes along the ground towards point.
Again sprayed down the leg side by Ngidi. Ali looks to flick but misses.
A fuller length around off, Ali is solid in his front foot defense.
Just wide of the fielder at leg gully. A fuller length on middle, Alam flicks this one uppishly but wide of the fielder at leg gully. They take single as the ball goes towards fine leg.
Fuller length around off, Alam shoulders arms to this one.
Good length around off, Alam works this in the gap at the mid-wicket area and comes back for a brace.
A fuller ball from Ngidi but sprayed down the leg. Alam looks to flick but misses.
Very full on off, Ali jams it out towards covers. Good yorker there by Rabada.
Bowls a shortish ball around off, Alam cuts this one towards deep point and takes a run.
Full around off, Alam comes forward and flicks this to the left of mid on.
Fuller length but outside off, Alam is not interested in playing that.
Good length around off, Alam defends this one out towards mid on.
Length ball in the channel outside off, left alone by Alam.
A good length ball to end! Gets it to rise from that area. Defended.
One more single! Once again a little too straight by a South African bowler, it is worked to fine leg for another single.
This one is wider outside leg, Alam does not fiddle with it.
Ngidi now is covering the ball with one hand as he runs in. He does not want the batter to know which side the shiny part is. He bowls it fuller and on middle, it is played back to the bowler.
Good running! Rotating the strike really nicely. On a length and around off, Ali pushes it towards cover. Calls for one immediately and takes it.
On the pads, this is worked down to fine leg for one. The visitors' bowlers have been a little too straight today.
Just over! On the fuller side, Alam works it but does so uppishly. He hits it well enough though to get it over Bavuma at square leg, towards the man in the deep for one.
Extremely full and on off, Alam jams it out towards mid on.
Back of a length and on off, Alam keeps it out.
A little too straight, it is clipped down to fine leg for one more run.
Continues to land it on a length and around off, blocked.
Catch it is the call but it is well wide! Rabada gets this one to tails back in from outside off. It ends up being onto the pads. Fawad works it uppishly but wide of square leg for one.
Back of a length and on the shorter side, Ali stands tall and pushes it to covers.
Another single! Once again the South African bowlers are guilty of bowling it way too straight, it is worked down to fine leg for one.
Uppish but wide! On the pads, there is extra bounce on this one. Azhar plays it well by taking a hand off the handle. It goes uppishly but wide of short square leg for one.
Close! This one tails back in from outside off. Ali lunges and looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Another one on the shorter side and angling into the batter, Ali stays back and tucks it easily to mid-wicket.
Shorter and on the body, Ali works it to mid-wicket.
Lungi Ngidi is into the attack now. 3-0-5-0 from him so far.
Length delivery to end and on off, Alam gets right behind the line and keeps it out.
Good running! On a length and around off, Ali drops it towards mid off and takes one.
Well bowled! Gets this one to shape away just a little. On a length and around off, Ali plays it late and towards mid off.
This time he times the pull well, waits for it and then plays it late through square leg for one.
On the shorter side, Alam is a touch early in the pull. The ball comes slow off the surface. It is mistimed towards mid-wicket.
On a length and well outside off, left alone.
Azhar would probably feel he misses out there! It is onto his pads, he works it but finds the fielder at square leg.
Solid! On a length and around off, this one comes back in from outside off. Ali gets right behind the line and blocks it to silly mid on.
Sharp! Changes his length and bangs it short. Ali ducks under it as he sees it early.
A little too straight, easy pickings as this is worked through square leg for another run.
Slightly fuller and outside off, Alam shoulders arms to this one.
Angled into the pads, Ali works it through square leg for one.
Length ball on off, tucked towards mid-wicket for nothing.

Ouch. That hit the gloves. A shortish ball around off, Alam looks to defend but gets hit on the gloves as his bottom hand comes off the bat. The ball falls on the leg side but short of the fielder at square leg.
That was close. A fullish ball around off, shapes in after pitching. Ali manages to put bat on the ball and turns this one towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Good short ball around off, Ali sways away and lets it go through to the keeper.
Length ball around off, Alam tucks this one softly towards mid-wicket and takes a quick single.
Good length around off, Alam comes on the front foot and blocks this out towards mid on.
Full again on middle, Alam flicks this one behind square on the on side for a single to bring up the 50 for Pakistan.
A length ball around off, shapes in after pitching. Alam looks to defend but gets an inside edge on his pads.
Length on off, Alam defends this off the back foot towards short mid on.
Nice timing. A fuller ball on middle, Ali plays this one with a straight bat down the ground. Rabada from mid on chases the ball and keeps the batters down to three.
Good ball. Full around middle, Ali flicks this one towards mid on. He almost loses his balance there.
FOUR! Nicely played. A length ball around off, Ali nicely guides it past the gully fielder for a boundary towards the third man region. A no ball too as Nortje has overstepped here.
Fullish around middle, Alam flicks it towards mid-wicket and calls his partner for a quick single.
Fullish around middle, Alam flicks this one towards deep square leg area and takes a run.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Length around off, Alam plays it on the off side for nothing.
Shortish around off, Alam pulls this in front of square on the leg side and comes back for a brace as the fielder in the deep cuts it off.
Length around off, Alam pushes it towards covers and shouts a loud 'no'.
Fullish around off, Ali taps it softly towards covers and calls his partner for a quick run.
On middle and leg, Ali flicks this one through the square leg area for a single.
Back of a length ball around off, Ali stands tall and plays it on the off side.

NOT OUT! A length ball around off, shapes in little after pitching. Ali looks to defend but the ball hits the pad first and then the bat. Some appeal but nothing from the umpire. They have taken the review. Replay shows that it was pad first but the impact was outside off and Ali survives.
Review time! An appeal for an LBW has been turned down and South Africa review. There seems to be bat involved and the impact seems outside off.
Fullish around off, Ali drives this one nicely towards covers for no run.
First runs for the day. A length around off, Ali pushes it towards cover-point where Maharaj misfields and allows the batters a brace.
Good length around off, Ali defends this out with a straight bat.
Nortje to bowl from the other end!
A length ball outside off, Alam lets it go. Maiden to start from Rabada.
Fuller around off, Alam flicks it towards mid on for no run.
Beaten again. A length ball around off, Alam looks to guide it to point but gets beaten by the low bounce there.
Length outside off, Alam lets it go through to the keeper.
Beaten. A length ball around off, straightens after pitching and goes past the outside edge of Alam's bat.
Rabada starts with a full length ball around off, Alam digs it out.

We are all set for the action to begin! The South African players are out there in the middle. Azhar Ali and Fawad Alam will resume their innings. Kagiso Rabada to start things first up. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Mike Haysman says it looks more like a Day 3 or a Day 4 pitch and it is going to be tough for the batters even today. Mentions there is not a lot of rough on the wicket but it still turns and the reverse swing is also going to make it tough for the batters to bat.

Pakistan on the other hand, need a partnership and they need one from the pair which will come out to bat now. A lot will depend on Azhar Ali, Fawad and Rizwan. They too will want a lead as they are the ones who’ll be batting last. Will we see the hosts fight back or will South Africa continue to dominate? All answers coming up shortly.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of this first Test between Pakistan and South Africa. An action-packed first day saw the bowlers dominating it with 14 wickets falling. The visitors have their noses slightly ahead at the moment. Their aim will be to keep chipping away at the wickets and will be pretty pleased with any sort of a lead.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

And he is the man the tourists would hope to snare as they resume play on Day 2. The deficit for the Pakistan is 187 and they are on a bit of a shaky ground here. Sure, they have decent batting to come, but given the collapses at the top, it remains to be seen if they can be resilient, at the bottom. Will Pakistan get past South Africa's first innings total or will Rabada and co. breathe fire again? Join us at 1000 Local (0500 GMT) on Wednesday, 27th January 2021, to find out. Until then, it is goodbye from our side...

Yasir Shah was the highlight, with 3 wickets to his name, while debutant Nauman Ali snared 2. The pacers had 3 wickets to their names. And then, Pakistan stepped out to bat, in their first innings. It was a horror start with the bat though, as they lost Abid Ali early and saw further collapses as well. In the end, they closed out Day 1, at 33/4, and probably have to thank the sun for setting down, rather than any of their batsmen. However, if one exception were to be made, one can say that Azhar Ali is gritting it out there.

A quick recap of the day's play - Saffas had won the toss and elected to bat first. They had a good strong start but lost Markram early. After that though, they could not construct a lasting partnership at all. The highest individual score from a South Africa batsman came from the blade of Dean Elgar, who scored a well-made 58. And that meant that the visitors could only post a total of 220. For Pakistan, with the ball, the spinners rose to the occasion.

Brilliant! Absolutely brilliant performance from South Africa, with the ball. We, the commentators, have been made to eat the humble pie. Looking at the first innings total of the South Africans (220), we thought that it was a poor effort from them in friendly batting conditions. But the conditions do not seem that batting-friendly, as their bowlers have done an even splendid job here.
On off, kept out off the front foot. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 1!
On off, Ali drives it towards covers but the fielder there does well to field it.
Length and around off, blocked out solidly off the front foot.
On of, pushed to covers.
Another fuller length ball on off, Azhar plays it out to mid-wicket.
Length and on off, tucked towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! Good shot. Good positive shot from Fawad Alam. FA can take a lot of confidence from that shot. Short length ball outside the off pole line, the left-hander rocks back and cuts it ferociously over point for a boundary.
On the pads, Azhar clips it to fine leg for a single.
Fawad is up and running. Good length outside the off pole line, Alam defends it to the off side and takes one.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his leg stump.
Fawad Alam strides out to the middle now.

OUT! BOWLED! Shaheen Afridi's stay at the crease is short lived. And the South Africans have all the reason to celebrate here. Not that it is a big wicket but because their bowling performance, in response to what has been a fairly low total, has been superb. Full length ball on middle and off, Shaheen comes forward in defence but misses and the ball goes through the gap between his bat and pad and crashes into the stumps behind.
On a good length, on the middle pole, Azhar flicks it to the mid-wicket region, for a single.
Flatter and around off, Afridi does well to keep it out off the back foot.
Tossed up on off, Afridi does well to play it off the front foot.
On off, Afridi blocks it out.
Who's in now? Hmm... Shaheen Afridi comes out to the middle, as the nightwatchman. Can he survive?

OUT! LBW! Maharaj just feeling like one after scalping Babar Azam in his first over itself. Tossed up on off, Azam looks to defend it off the front foot but is beaten to get rapped on the pads. There is an appeal and the umpire raises his finger to give the marching orders to Azam. Hang on... Azam has signalled 'T' after consulting his partner. Replays roll in and it is a fair delivery reckons the third umpire as the front on spin vision comes on. Looks to be plumb but lets see if he has got any bat there. The Ultra Edge comes on and it shows a flat line. Now the Ball Tracker and it shows Three Reds. Pakistan's worst fears have come true.
Flatter and around off, Azam punches it off the back foot towards covers.
Tossed up on off, kept out safely by Babar.
Keshav Maharaj is into the attack.
Short length ball, outside the off pole line, hit to point.
Short length delivery, outside the off pole, dabbed to the man at point.
Full length delivery around off, it is blocked to the off side.
This time it is wide of the man at mid-wicket and allows the batsmen to take a single.
On a good length and on middle, it is flicked well but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Good length, around off, defended.
On a fuller length and on middle, driven down the ground towards mid on to see off the over.
And Azhar Ali continues to leave the good length ball outside his off pole.
Full and on the pads, Azam flicks it all along the carpet towards mid-wicket and gets a single on offer.
On a good length and around middle and leg, Azam helps it on its way to square leg.
Length and outside off, Azam lets this one go through to the keeper.
Length and around off, Azam defends it off the back foot towards the on side.
Full length delivery outside off, driven to covers.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
Shortish delivery outside off, it is punched off the back foot through the covers, for a single.
Full length delivery around off, it is driven to covers.
On the pads, clipped down to fine leg for one.
Full length ball around off, played towards mid off.
Length and on off, Azam once again is on the back foot as he defends the ball.
Good length and on off, Azam blocks it out from within the crease this time.
On a length and around off, Ali hops and tucks it towards square leg and scampers for a single with ease.
Length and on off, flicked straight towards mid-wicket this time by Azhar. He is struggling to find the gaps.
Length and on off, blocked off the back foot towards mid on by Ali.
Length and outisde off, Ali lets it be. It is a No Ball too. Ngidi has overstepped there.
Length ball on leg, Azam flicks it off his pads towards fine leg for a single.
Full length delivery on middle, played to square leg.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
Shortish and on middle, that is flicked through square leg, off the back foot, for a single.
Shortish length ball outside off, came a bit slower than Babar would have anticipated. He waits and waits before stabbing it to short third man.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Full length delivery on middle, flicked to mid-wicket.
Full and angled on middle, Azhar flicks it but cannot beat the man at mid-wicket.
On off, Ali pushes it off the back foot towards mid on.
Full and angled on the pads of Babar, Azam clips it towards fine leg and takes a single this time.
Length and on off, Azam gets right behind the line of the ball and defends it to the mid on region.
Fuller and on off, Babar now squeezes this ball to the point region.
Length and on the pads, Azam flicks it to the man at square leg.
Good length and around off, it is defended.
An on-drive from Ali but this one finds the man at mid on perfectly.
Shortish length delivery on middle, Babar rocks back and clips it through square leg for a single.
Short length delivery outside the off pole, Babar rides the bounce and taps it to point.
Another full length ball which has been driven down to mid off.
Full length delivery around the off pole, played down to mid off.
Good length ball and outside off, Ali leaves it for the keeper to gobble it up.
Back of a length ball on off, Ali blocks it out off the back foot towards the leg side.
Good length and outside off omce again from Nortje, Ali leaves it one more time for the keeper to do the rest.
Back of  length and outside off, Ali quickly sees the line of the ball and then makes a leave.
Full and on off, pushed down to mid off this time.
Full and outside off, Azhar Ali covers his sticks and lets the ball through to the keeper.
Outside off, left alone.
NO BALL! Kagiso has overstepped here. Full and outside off, it is driven to covers.
Good length ball around off, Babar defends it.

OUT! CAUGHT! Simple catch. The debutant has to make the long walk back here. Short length delivery around off, Imran looks to pull at that but gets a top edge there. It goes high in the air near the square leg region where the substitute fielder is waiting like a hawk. Pouches onto it safely as soon as it lands down.
Full length ball outside off, Azhar drives it through the covers and picks up two.
Good length delivery around the off pole, Azhar defends it.
Full length delivery around off, Imran drives it through the covers for a single.
Good length ball on the pads, Imran works it down to fine leg for a couple. Hang on, Kagiso has overstepped here. No ball called.
Good length and around off, Ali defends it out off the front foot. He has faced 6 balls so far and is yet to get off the mark here.
Fuller and on off, Imran clips it through mid-wicket and crosses over for a single.
Length and around off, Butt lifts his willow and makes way for the ball to go and settle into the mitts of the keeper.

FOUR! First boundary for the debutant and he will always remember this moment and cherish it. Short of good length on middle, Butt swivels and then pulls it through mid-wicket and the ball races to the fence there.
Good length and outside off, Butt sees the ball and then shoulders arms to it.
Length and around off, Butt is solid in defence. The debutant looks in good shape here.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Good ball there from Kagiso. He bowls a short ball and Azhar Ali does equally well to duck under that one. Good cricket overall.
Good length delivery on off, Azhar blocks it.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Who will walk out to the middle now? Azhar Ali is the new man in.

OUT! Cleaned up! There comes the first breakthrough for South Africa. An early breakthrough and yes, they are very much in the game here. Full length delivery around off, Abid strides forward and looks to drive it through the covers, on the off side. But he ends up getting an inside edge there. Sometimes, the ball goes past the stumps and to the fine leg region. But this was not one of those times. It crashes into the stumps and Ali has to make the long walk back here.
Full and on off, driven down to mid off by Butt.
Length and on off, Butt defends it out.
Good length and on off, Butt blocks it to covers.
Length and on off, Abid Ali punches it through covers and gets a single.
Length and on the pads, Butt tucks it towards the square leg region and gets a single. First runs for him in Test cricket.

Pakistan and Abid Ali are underway! Length ball on off, Abid looks to defend it but the ball goes off his outside edge and runs through the vacant gully region. Maharaj from slips runs towards the ball and keeps the batsmen down to three runs.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Bouncer from Kagiso, Imran ducks under it.
BEATEN! This is superb stuff from Rabada. Good length ball around off, moving away. It shapes away in such a manner that it beats the outside edge of Butt as the debutant strode forward to defend.
Full and around off, driven down to mid off.
PLAY AND A MISS! That was an absolute beauty there. Kagiso runs in and bowls a full length delivery around off, Imran comes forward in defence but misses.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Length and around off, Ali defends it out peacefully. A maiden once again.
Good shot! Not for runs though! Short and wide outside off, Ali cuts it off the back foot but hits it straight to the man at point. A millimeter on either side and it would have been a boundary.
A short one from Nortje and Ali decides not to fiddle with it early in the innings as he ducks under it.
Fuller in length and around off, Abid comes on the front foot and creams the drive but fails to beat the man at covers.
Good length and on off, Ali is happy to block it out off the back foot.
Full and around off, Ali drives it but fails to pierce the gap at covers.
Who will bowl from the other end for South Africa? It is Anrich Nortje.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one which was outside off through. A maiden over to start then, for Rabada and South Africa.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
Play and a miss! Good ball there from Rabada. Lands it full and outside off, Imran comes forward and goes for the drive but ends up missing it.
Down the leg side and Imran lets that be.
Another one in the channel outside off and the batsman shoulders arms to this one.
The first ball from Rabada is outside off and it is left for the keeper to collect.
